The processor that receives the claim
questions.explain: The Bank Identification Number (BIN) routes the claim to the correct processor. The cardholder ID identifies the member, and the person code identifies which family member is receiving the prescription.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (third party billing)
questions.q: What does the person code on a prescription insurance card identify?
options: The pharmacy that submitted the claim
Which covered family member is receiving the fill
The doctor who wrote the prescription
questions.explain: The person code distinguishes the cardholder from a spouse or dependents who share the same ID number. A wrong person code is a frequent reason for rejected claims. The PCN is a separate field used with the BIN for routing.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (coordination of benefits)
questions.q: A patient has two prescription plans. What is the correct billing order?
options: Bill the secondary plan first, then the primary
Bill the primary plan first, then the secondary
Bill both plans at the same time for full price
questions.explain: Coordination of benefits means the primary plan is billed first, and the remaining balance is then sent to the secondary plan. Billing out of order or billing both for the full amount causes rejected or incorrect payments.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (insurance terms)
questions.q: What is a deductible in a prescription benefit?
options: The fixed fee paid each time a drug is filled
The percentage of the cost the patient shares
The plan's list of covered drugs
What is paid before the plan starts paying
questions.explain: A deductible is what the patient pays each benefit period before the plan begins to pay. A copay is a fixed amount per fill, coinsurance is a percentage of the cost, and the formulary is the list of covered drugs.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (insurance terms)
questions.q: In pharmacy benefits, what is a formulary?
options: The list of drugs a plan covers
A book of tested compounding recipes
A record of controlled drug destruction
A list of drugs on recall
questions.explain: A formulary lists the drugs a health plan covers or a hospital stocks, often arranged in tiers that set the patient's cost. A drug not on the formulary may need a prior authorization or a switch to a covered alternative.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (inventory management)
questions.q: When putting away a wholesaler order, where should newly received stock with a later expiration date be placed?
options: In front of the stock already on the shelf
On a separate shelf in another aisle
Behind the stock already on the shelf
In the refrigerator to extend dating
questions.explain: Stock rotation places the product with the earliest expiration in front so it is used first, and newer stock goes behind. This reduces waste from expired drugs. Refrigerating a room temperature product does not extend its expiration.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (inventory management)
questions.q: In pharmacy inventory, what is a par level?
options: The highest price allowed for an item
The number of refills left on a prescription
The cost difference between brand and generic
The amount of an item to keep on hand
questions.explain: A par level is the target quantity to keep in stock; when inventory falls to the reorder point, enough is ordered to return to par. It is set from usage history and lead time and has nothing to do with pricing or refills.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (inventory management)
questions.q: What is a perpetual inventory?
options: A full count done once every two years
A count updated with each receipt and sale
A list of drugs the pharmacy never stocks at all
A record of only expired items
questions.explain: A perpetual inventory updates the on hand count continuously as products are received and dispensed. Many pharmacies keep one for Schedule II drugs. The biennial inventory is a separate count required by the DEA every two years.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (inventory management)
questions.q: What usually happens to short dated or expired stock that is eligible for credit?
options: It is sold at a discount to patients
It is given to staff for personal use
It goes to a reverse distributor
It is returned to the shelf after relabeling
questions.explain: Pharmacies use reverse distributors to return expired or unwanted products for manufacturer credit or proper disposal. Dispensing, discounting or relabeling expired product is not allowed. Controlled substances need extra documentation.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (customer service)
questions.q: A patient is upset about a high copay. Which response is most appropriate for the technician?
options: Listen calmly and offer to check options with the pharmacist
Tell the patient the price cannot be discussed
Argue that the plan sets prices, not the pharmacy
Lower the price on your own to end the dispute
questions.explain: Good service means listening, staying calm and offering help, such as checking for a covered alternative, a coupon program or a 90 day supply, with the pharmacist or prescriber as needed. Arguing or changing prices without authority makes things worse.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (customer service)
questions.q: A patient who speaks limited English needs help at the counter. What is the best approach?
options: Use the pharmacy's interpreter or language line service
Speak louder and more slowly in English
Ask a child in the family to translate
Give the bag without explaining anything
questions.explain: Professional interpreter services give accurate communication and protect privacy. Speaking louder does not improve understanding, and relying on family members, especially children, risks errors and breaches of confidentiality.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (confidentiality)
questions.q: Which practice protects patient privacy at the pharmacy counter?
options: Reading the full drug list aloud to confirm
Leaving filled bags open on the counter
Speaking quietly and keeping labels out of view
Calling out diagnoses across the waiting area
questions.explain: HIPAA requires reasonable safeguards for protected health information. Lowering the voice, using the consultation area and keeping labels and screens out of public view reduce incidental disclosures. Announcing drug names or diagnoses aloud exposes PHI.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (workflow)
questions.q: Which sequence reflects a typical community pharmacy workflow for a new prescription?
options: Filling, intake, pickup, data entry, verification
Intake, data entry, filling, pharmacist verification, pickup
Pickup, verification, filling, intake, data entry
Data entry, pickup, intake, filling, verification
questions.explain: A prescription is received and checked at intake, entered and billed, filled, verified by the pharmacist and then released to the patient with counseling. Pickup before verification would allow unchecked medication to reach the patient.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (third party billing)
questions.q: A filled prescription was billed to insurance but never picked up. Before returning the medication to stock, what must be done?
options: Bill the patient for the full price
Send the claim to the secondary plan
Reverse the claim with the plan
questions.explain: If a billed prescription is not dispensed, the claim must be reversed so the plan is not charged for something the patient never received. Leaving it paid misrepresents the dispensing and can be treated as fraud in an audit.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (technician and pharmacist tasks)
questions.q: A patient asks the technician whether to take a missed dose now or skip it. What should the technician do?
options: Tell the patient to double the next dose
Advise skipping all doses for the day
Have the pharmacist answer the question
Look it up online and answer directly
questions.explain: Advice on missed doses depends on the drug and the patient, so it requires the pharmacist's judgment. Technicians do not give clinical advice. Doubling doses can cause harm for many medications.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (insurance programs)
questions.q: Medicare Part D covers which type of benefit?
questions.explain: Part D is the Medicare outpatient prescription drug benefit, provided through private plans. Part A covers inpatient hospital care, and Part B covers physician services and some drugs given in clinics. Custodial long term care is generally not covered by Medicare.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (rejected claims)
questions.q: A claim rejects for 'Quantity limit exceeded'. What does this indicate?
options: The patient's date of birth does not match
The prescriber is not licensed in the state
The drug requires refrigeration during shipping
The amount billed exceeds what the plan allows for that time period
questions.explain: Plans set quantity limits per fill or per period for many drugs. Options include billing the allowed quantity, checking that days supply and quantity were entered correctly, or having the prescriber request an exception. A date of birth mismatch gives a different rejection.

questions.ref: ExCPT test plan 2023, Role, Responsibilities and General Duties (patient profiles)
questions.q: When creating a profile for a new patient, which information is essential to collect?
options: Favorite store hours and parking needs
Allergies, date of birth and current medications
The patient's employer and job title
The patient's preferred brand of vitamins
questions.explain: Allergies, date of birth, other medications, conditions and insurance details allow accurate billing and allow the pharmacist to screen for allergies and interactions. Employer details are not needed for dispensing.
